sanskrit: yad idaṃ cāpalān mūrteḥ sarvam etac cikīrṣati manaḥ prati sutīkṣṇāgrān ahaṃ mokṣyāmi sāyakān
english: Since out of its fickleness the embodied mind desires to do all this, I shall loose arrows of keenest point against the mind itself.

sanskrit: mana uvāca neme bāṇās tariṣyanti mām alarka kathaṃ cana tavaiva marma bhetsyanti bhinnamarmā mariṣyasi
english: The mind said: These arrows of yours, Alarka, shall in no way pass through me; they will only pierce your own vital parts, and with your vitals pierced you shall die.

sanskrit: anyān bāṇān samīkṣasva yais tvaṃ māṃ sūdayiṣyasi tac chrutvā sa vicintyātha tato vacanam abravīt
english: Look rather for other arrows by which you might destroy me. Hearing this, he reflected and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: alarka uvāca āghrāya subahūn gandhāṃs tān eva pratigṛdhyati tasmād ghrāṇaṃ prati śarān pratimokṣyāmy ahaṃ śitān
english: Alarka said: Having smelled the manifold scents, it craves after those very scents; therefore I shall loose my sharpened shafts against the sense of smell.

sanskrit: ghrāṇa uvāca neme bāṇās tariṣyanti mām alarka kathaṃ cana tavaiva marma bhetsyanti bhinnamarmā mariṣyasi
english: The sense of smell said: These arrows of yours, Alarka, shall in no way pass through me; they will only pierce your own vital parts, and with your vitals pierced you shall die.

sanskrit: anyān bāṇān samīkṣasva yais tvaṃ māṃ sūdayiṣyasi tac chrutvā sa vicintyātha tato vacanam abravīt
english: Look rather for other arrows by which you might destroy me. Hearing this, he reflected and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: alarka uvāca iyaṃ svādūn rasān bhuktvā tān eva pratigṛdhyati tasmāj jihvāṃ prati śarān pratimokṣyāmy ahaṃ śitān
english: Alarka said: Having enjoyed the sweet tastes, it craves after those very tastes; therefore I shall loose my sharpened shafts against the tongue.

sanskrit: jihvovāca neme bāṇās tariṣyanti mām alarka kathaṃ cana tavaiva marma bhetsyanti bhinnamarmā mariṣyasi
english: The tongue said: These arrows of yours, Alarka, shall in no way pass through me; they will only pierce your own vital parts, and with your vitals pierced you shall die.

sanskrit: anyān bāṇān samīkṣasva yais tvaṃ māṃ sūdayiṣyasi tac chrutvā sa vicintyātha tato vacanam abravīt
english: Look rather for other arrows by which you might destroy me. Hearing this, he reflected and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: alarka uvāca spṛṣṭvā tvag vividhān sparśāṃs tān eva pratigṛdhyati tasmāt tvacaṃ pāṭayiṣye vividhaiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: Alarka said: Having touched the manifold textures, the skin craves after those very contacts; therefore I shall rend the skin with my many heron-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: tvag uvāca neme bāṇās tariṣyanti mām alarka kathaṃ cana tavaiva marma bhetsyanti bhinnamarmā mariṣyasi
english: The skin said: These arrows of yours, Alarka, shall in no way pass through me; they will only pierce your own vital parts, and with your vitals pierced you shall die.

sanskrit: anyān bāṇān samīkṣasva yais tvaṃ māṃ sūdayiṣyasi tac chrutvā sa vicintyātha tato vacanam abravīt
english: Look rather for other arrows by which you might destroy me. Hearing this, he reflected and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: alarka uvāca śrutvā vai vividhāñ śabdāṃs tān eva pratigṛdhyati tasmāc chrotraṃ prati śarān pratimokṣyāmy ahaṃ śitān
english: Alarka said: Having heard the manifold sounds, it craves after those very sounds; therefore I shall loose my sharpened shafts against the sense of hearing.

sanskrit: śrotra uvāca neme bāṇās tariṣyanti mām alarka kathaṃ cana tavaiva marma bhetsyanti tato hāsyasi jīvitam
english: The ear said: These arrows of yours, Alarka, shall in no way pass through me; they will only pierce your own vital parts, and thereby you shall give up your life.

sanskrit: anyān bāṇān samīkṣasva yais tvaṃ māṃ sūdayiṣyasi tac chrutvā sa vicintyātha tato vacanam abravīt
english: Look rather for other arrows by which you might destroy me. Hearing this, he reflected and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: alarka uvāca dṛṣṭvā vai vividhān bhāvāṃs tān eva pratigṛdhyati tasmāc cakṣuḥ prati śarān pratimokṣyāmy ahaṃ śitān
english: Alarka said: Having seen the manifold forms, it craves after those very objects; therefore I shall loose my sharpened shafts against the eye.

sanskrit: cakṣur uvāca neme bāṇās tariṣyanti mām alarka kathaṃ cana tavaiva marma bhetsyanti bhinnamarmā mariṣyasi
english: The eye said: These arrows of yours, Alarka, shall in no way pass through me; they will only pierce your own vital parts, and with your vitals pierced you shall die.

sanskrit: anyān bāṇān samīkṣasva yais tvaṃ māṃ sūdayiṣyasi tac chrutvā sa vicintyātha tato vacanam abravīt
english: Look rather for other arrows by which you might destroy me. Hearing this, he reflected and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: alarka uvāca iyaṃ niṣṭhā bahuvidhā prajñayā tv adhyavasyati tasmād buddhiṃ prati śarān pratimokṣyāmy ahaṃ śitān
english: Alarka said: This faculty of resolve, manifold in kind, deliberates through the understanding; therefore I shall loose my sharpened shafts against the intellect.

sanskrit: buddhir uvāca neme bāṇās tariṣyanti mām alarka kathaṃ cana tavaiva marma bhetsyanti bhinnamarmā mariṣyasi
english: The intellect said: These arrows of yours, Alarka, shall in no way pass through me; they will only pierce your own vital parts, and with your vitals pierced you shall die.

sanskrit: pitara ūcuḥ tato 'larkas tapo ghoram āsthāyātha suduṣkaram nādhyagacchat paraṃ śaktyā bāṇam eteṣu saptasu susamāhitacetās tu tato 'cintayata prabhuḥ
english: The fathers said: Then Alarka, taking up a terrible and most arduous penance, could find with all his might no arrow to use against these seven; and so, with his mind fully composed, the lord pondered.

sanskrit: sa vicintya ciraṃ kālam alarko dvijasattama nādhyagacchat paraṃ śreyo yogān matimatāṃ varaḥ
english: Having reflected for a long while, O best of the twice-born, Alarka, foremost of the wise, found no higher good than yoga.

sanskrit: sa ekāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā niścalo yogam āsthitaḥ indriyāṇi jaghānāśu bāṇenaikena vīryavān yogenātmānam āviśya saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ yayau
english: Making his mind one-pointed and unwavering, he took his stand in yoga; the hero swiftly slew the senses with a single arrow, and entering into the Self through yoga he attained the highest perfection.

sanskrit: vismitaś cāpi rājarṣir imāṃ gāthāṃ jagāda ha aho kaṣṭaṃ yad asmābhiḥ pūrvaṃ rājyam anuṣṭhitam iti paścān mayā jñātaṃ yogān nāsti paraṃ sukham
english: And the royal sage, marveling, uttered this verse: Alas, how grievous that we formerly devoted ourselves to kingship! Only afterward did I learn that there is no happiness higher than yoga.

sanskrit: iti tvam api jānīhi rāma mā kṣatriyāñ jahi tapo ghoram upātiṣṭha tataḥ śreyo 'bhipatsyase
english: Know this too, O Rāma: do not slay the Kṣatriyas. Undertake a terrible penance, and thereby you shall attain the supreme good.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tapo ghoraṃ jāmadagnyaḥ pitāmahaiḥ āsthitaḥ sumahābhāgo yayau siddhiṃ ca durgamām
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Thus addressed by his ancestors, the son of Jamadagni, exceedingly blessed, took up a terrible penance and attained a perfection hard to reach.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca trayo vai ripavo loke nava vai guṇataḥ smṛtāḥ harṣaḥ stambho 'bhimānaś ca trayas te sāttvikā guṇāḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa said: In the world there are three foes, held to be nine by their qualities. Elation, stubbornness, and conceit—these three are the sāttvika qualities.

sanskrit: śokaḥ krodho 'tisaṃrambho rājasās te guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ svapnas tandrī ca mohaś ca trayas te tāmasā guṇāḥ
english: Grief, anger, and excessive impetuosity—these are reckoned the rājasa qualities. Sleep, drowsiness, and delusion—these three are the tāmasa qualities.

sanskrit: etān nikṛtya dhṛtimān bāṇasaṃghair atandritaḥ jetuṃ parān utsahate praśāntātmā jitendriyaḥ
english: Having cut these down with volleys of arrows, the steadfast and tireless man, his self serene and his senses mastered, is able to conquer his foes.

sanskrit: atra gāthāḥ kīrtayanti purākalpavido janāḥ ambarīṣeṇa yā gītā rājñā rājyaṃ praśāsatā
english: On this matter those who know the ancient lore recite verses, those which were sung by King Ambarīṣa as he governed his kingdom.

sanskrit: samudīrṇeṣu doṣeṣu vadhyamāneṣu sādhuṣu jagrāha tarasā rājyam ambarīṣa iti śrutiḥ
english: When the vices had risen up and the good were being slain, Ambarīṣa seized the kingdom by main force—so runs the tradition.

sanskrit: sa nigṛhya mahādoṣān sādhūn samabhipūjya ca jagāma mahatīṃ siddhiṃ gāthāṃ cemāṃ jagāda ha
english: Having subdued the great vices and duly honored the good, he attained a high perfection and uttered this verse.

sanskrit: bhūyiṣṭhaṃ me jitā doṣā nihatāḥ sarvaśatravaḥ eko doṣo 'vaśiṣṭas tu vadhyaḥ sa na hato mayā
english: For the most part my vices are conquered and all my enemies slain; but one vice remains, which deserves to be killed, and which I have not yet killed.

sanskrit: yena yukto jantur ayaṃ vaitṛṣṇyaṃ nādhigacchati tṛṣṇārta iva nimnāni dhāvamāno na budhyate
english: Possessed by it, this creature never attains freedom from craving; tormented by thirst, running toward the low places, he does not come to his senses.

sanskrit: akāryam api yeneha prayuktaḥ sevate naraḥ taṃ lobham asibhis tīkṣṇair nikṛntantaṃ nikṛntata
english: That greed which, driving a man, makes him pursue even what ought not to be done—cut it down, even as it cuts you down, with sharp swords.

sanskrit: lobhād dhi jāyate tṛṣṇā tataś cintā prasajyate sa lipsamāno labhate bhūyiṣṭhaṃ rājasān guṇān
english: For from greed is born craving, and from that anxiety follows; the man who lusts to acquire gathers in abundance the rājasa qualities.

sanskrit: sa tair guṇaiḥ saṃhatadehabandhanaḥ; punaḥ punar jāyati karma cehate janmakṣaye bhinnavikīrṇadehaḥ; punar mṛtyuṃ gacchati janmani sve
english: Bound in the bondage of the body by those qualities, he is born again and again and toils at action; when his life ends his body is broken and scattered, and in his next birth he goes once more to death.

sanskrit: tasmād enaṃ samyag avekṣya lobhaṃ; nigṛhya dhṛtyātmani rājyam icchet etad rājyaṃ nānyad astīti vidyād; yas tv atra rājā vijito mamaikaḥ
english: Therefore, having rightly perceived this greed and subdued it with firmness, let a man seek sovereignty over himself. Let him know that this is the true kingdom and there is no other; for here within, that one king has been vanquished by me.

sanskrit: iti rājñāmbarīṣeṇa gāthā gītā yaśasvinā ādhirājyaṃ puraskṛtya lobham ekaṃ nikṛntatā
english: Thus was this verse sung by the illustrious King Ambarīṣa, who, setting supreme sovereignty before him, cut down greed alone.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam brāhmaṇasya ca saṃvādaṃ janakasya ca bhāmini
english: The brāhmaṇa said: On this too, O fair lady, they recite this ancient story, the dialogue between a brāhmaṇa and Janaka.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaṃ janako rājā sannaṃ kasmiṃś cid āgame viṣaye me na vastavyam iti śiṣṭyartham abravīt
english: To a brāhmaṇa who had settled there on the strength of some scriptural authority, King Janaka said, by way of discipline: You must not dwell within my domain.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratyuvācātha brāhmaṇo rājasattamam ācakṣva viṣayaṃ rājan yāvāṃs tava vaśe sthitaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the brāhmaṇa answered that best of kings: Tell me, O king, how far the domain extends that stands within your power.

sanskrit: so 'nyasya viṣaye rājño vastum icchāmy ahaṃ vibho vacas te kartum icchāmi yathāśāstraṃ mahīpate
english: I wish to dwell, O mighty one, within the domain of another king; I wish to obey your word in accord with the scriptures, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tadā rājā brāhmaṇena yaśasvinā muhur uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasya na sa taṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Thus addressed by the illustrious brāhmaṇa, the king then sighed hot sighs again and again, and made him no answer.

sanskrit: tam āsīnaṃ dhyāyamānaṃ rājānam amitaujasam kaśmalaṃ sahasāgacchad bhānumantam iva grahaḥ
english: As that king of boundless might sat there absorbed in thought, a faintness suddenly came over him, as an eclipse overtakes the radiant sun.

sanskrit: samāśvāsya tato rājā vyapete kaśmale tadā tato muhūrtād iva taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then the king, recovering himself when the faintness had passed, after a moment spoke these words to the brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmahe rājye vaśye janapade sati viṣayaṃ nādhigacchāmi vicinvan pṛthivīm imām
english: Though the kingdom of my fathers and forefathers is mine, and the people obedient, yet, searching this whole earth, I can find no domain that is truly my own.

sanskrit: nādhyagacchaṃ yadā pṛthvyāṃ mithilā mārgitā mayā nādhyagacchaṃ yadā tasyāṃ svaprajā mārgitā mayā
english: When I searched the earth I did not find it; when I searched within Mithilā I did not find it; when I sought my own subjects therein, I did not find it.

sanskrit: nādhyagacchaṃ yadā tāsu tadā me kaśmalo 'bhavat tato me kaśmalasyānte matiḥ punar upasthitā
english: When I could not find it among them, then this faintness came upon me; but when the faintness ended, my understanding returned to me.

sanskrit: tayā na viṣayaṃ manye sarvo vā viṣayo mama ātmāpi cāyaṃ na mama sarvā vā pṛthivī mama uṣyatāṃ yāvad utsāho bhujyatāṃ yāvad iṣyate
english: By that understanding I judge that no domain is mine, or else the whole world is my domain; even this self is not mine, or else the whole earth is mine. Dwell here as long as you have the will, and enjoy as much as you desire.

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmahe rājye vaśye janapade sati brūhi kāṃ buddhim āsthāya mamatvaṃ varjitaṃ tvayā
english: Though the kingdom of your fathers and forefathers is yours, and the people obedient, tell me—resting on what conviction have you renounced the sense of 'mine'?

sanskrit: kāṃ vā buddhiṃ viniścitya sarvo vai viṣayas tava nāvaiṣi viṣayaṃ yena sarvo vā viṣayas tava
english: Or having settled on what conviction is it that all becomes your domain—the conviction by which you do not regard any as your domain, and yet all becomes your domain?

sanskrit: janaka uvāca antavanta ihārambhā viditāḥ sarvakarmasu nādhyagaccham ahaṃ yasmān mamedam iti yad bhavet
english: Janaka said: In all undertakings here the works are known to be finite; therefore I could find nothing of which I might say, 'This is mine.'

sanskrit: kasyedam iti kasya svam iti vedavacas tathā nādhyagaccham ahaṃ buddhyā mamedam iti yad bhavet
english: 'Whose is this?' 'Whose is the property?'—so run the words of the Veda; reasoning thus with my intellect, I could find nothing of which I might say, 'This is mine.'

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ viniścitya mamatvaṃ varjitaṃ mayā śṛṇu buddhiṃ tu yāṃ jñātvā sarvatra viṣayo mama
english: Having settled on this conviction, I have renounced the sense of 'mine'. Now hear the conviction by knowing which all things everywhere become my domain.

sanskrit: nāham ātmārtham icchāmi gandhān ghrāṇagatān api tasmān me nirjitā bhūmir vaśe tiṣṭhati nityadā
english: I do not desire even the scents that reach the nose for my own sake; therefore earth is conquered by me and abides forever in my power.

sanskrit: nāham ātmārtham icchāmi rasān āsye 'pi vartataḥ āpo me nirjitās tasmād vaśe tiṣṭhanti nityadā
english: I do not desire even the tastes present in my mouth for my own sake; therefore the waters are conquered by me and abide forever in my power.

sanskrit: nāham ātmārtham icchāmi rūpaṃ jyotiś ca cakṣuṣā tasmān me nirjitaṃ jyotir vaśe tiṣṭhati nityadā
english: I do not desire form and light through the eye for my own sake; therefore light is conquered by me and abides forever in my power.

sanskrit: nāham ātmārtham icchāmi sparśāṃs tvaci gatāś ca ye tasmān me nirjito vāyur vaśe tiṣṭhati nityadā
english: I do not desire for my own sake the contacts that reach the skin; therefore the wind is conquered by me and abides forever in my power.

sanskrit: nāham ātmārtham icchāmi śabdāñ śrotragatān api tasmān me nirjitāḥ śabdā vaśe tiṣṭhanti nityadā
english: I do not desire even the sounds that reach the ear for my own sake; therefore sounds are conquered by me and abide forever in my power.

sanskrit: nāham ātmārtham icchāmi mano nityaṃ manontare mano me nirjitaṃ tasmād vaśe tiṣṭhati nityadā
english: I do not desire the mind for my own sake, ever fixed within the inner mind; therefore the mind is conquered by me and abides forever in my power.

sanskrit: devebhyaś ca pitṛbhyaś ca bhūtebhyo 'tithibhiḥ saha ityarthaṃ sarva eveme samārambhā bhavanti vai
english: For the gods, for the fathers, for created beings, together with guests—it is for this purpose that all these undertakings exist.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya janakaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ punar abravīt tvajjijñāsārtham adyeha viddhi māṃ dharmam āgatam
english: Then, smiling, the brāhmaṇa spoke again to Janaka: Know that I have come here today, in the guise of dharma itself, to test you.

sanskrit: tvam asya brahmanābhasya buddhyārasyānivartinaḥ sattvaneminiruddhasya cakrasyaikaḥ pravartakaḥ
english: You alone are the turner of this wheel whose hub is Brahman, whose spokes are the intellect, which never turns back, and which is held firm by the rim of sattva.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca nāhaṃ tathā bhīru carāmi loke; tathā tvaṃ māṃ tarkayase svabuddhyā vipro 'smi mukto 'smi vanecaro 'smi; gṛhasthadharmā brahmacārī tathāsmi
english: The brāhmaṇa said: I do not move in the world, O timid one, in the way you suppose me by your own reasoning. I am a brāhmaṇa, I am liberated, I am a forest-dweller; I am also a householder by duty, and a celibate student as well.

sanskrit: nāham asmi yathā māṃ tvaṃ paśyase cakṣuṣā śubhe mayā vyāptam idaṃ sarvaṃ yat kiṃ cij jagatīgatam
english: I am not, O fair one, as you behold me with your eye; by me is pervaded all this, whatever exists upon the earth.

sanskrit: ye ke cij jantavo loke jaṅgamāḥ sthāvarāś ca ha teṣāṃ mām antakaṃ viddhi dārūṇām iva pāvakam
english: Whatever creatures there are in the world, moving and unmoving, know me to be their ender, as fire is the ender of pieces of wood.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ pṛthivyāṃ sarvasyām atha vāpi triviṣṭape tathā buddhir iyaṃ vetti buddhir eva dhanaṃ mama
english: Sovereignty over all the earth, or even over heaven itself—this intellect knows it for what it is; the intellect alone is my wealth.

sanskrit: ekaḥ panthā brāhmaṇānāṃ yena gacchanti tadvidaḥ gṛheṣu vanavāseṣu guruvāseṣu bhikṣuṣu liṅgair bahubhir avyagrair ekā buddhir upāsyate
english: One is the path of the brāhmaṇas, by which those who know it go—in homes, in forest dwellings, in the houses of teachers, among mendicants; through many tokens, unconfused, the one intellect is worshiped.

sanskrit: nānāliṅgāśramasthānāṃ yeṣāṃ buddhiḥ śamātmikā te bhāvam ekam āyānti saritaḥ sāgaraṃ yathā
english: Those of diverse tokens and stations of life, whose intellect is of the nature of tranquility, arrive at one and the same state, as rivers come to the sea.

sanskrit: buddhyāyaṃ gamyate mārgaḥ śarīreṇa na gamyate ādyantavanti karmāṇi śarīraṃ karmabandhanam
english: This path is traversed by the intellect; it is not traversed by the body. Actions have a beginning and an end, and the body is the bondage of action.

sanskrit: tasmāt te subhage nāsti paralokakṛtaṃ bhayam madbhāvabhāvaniratā mamaivātmānam eṣyasi
english: Therefore, O blessed one, you have no fear concerning the world beyond; devoted to dwelling in my being, you shall come to my very Self.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇy uvāca nedam alpātmanā śakyaṃ vedituṃ nākṛtātmanā bahu cālpaṃ ca saṃkṣiptaṃ viplutaṃ ca mataṃ mama
english: The brāhmaṇa woman said: This cannot be understood by one of little soul, nor by one whose self is unperfected. My understanding finds it at once vast and slight, condensed and yet bewildering.

sanskrit: upāyaṃ tu mama brūhi yenaiṣā labhyate matiḥ tan manye kāraṇatamaṃ yata eṣā pravartate
english: But tell me the means by which this understanding is attained; that I deem the chief cause from which it arises.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca araṇīṃ brāhmaṇīṃ viddhi gurur asyottarāraṇiḥ tapaḥśrute 'bhimathnīto jñānāgnir jāyate tataḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Know the lower fire-stick to be the brāhmaṇa-power, and the teacher to be its upper stick; when austerity and sacred learning churn them together, from this is born the fire of knowledge.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇy uvāca yad idaṃ brahmaṇo liṅgaṃ kṣetrajñam iti saṃjñitam grahītuṃ yena tac chakyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tasya tat kva nu
english: The brāhmaṇa woman said: This token of Brahman that is named the knower of the field—by what mark can it be grasped, and where indeed is that mark of it?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca aliṅgo nirguṇaś caiva kāraṇaṃ nāsya vidyate upāyam eva vakṣyāmi yena gṛhyeta vā na vā
english: The brāhmaṇa said: It is without token and without quality, and no cause of it is known. Yet I shall tell the means by which it may be grasped, or may not.

sanskrit: samyag apy upadiṣṭaś ca bhramarair iva lakṣyate karmabuddhir abuddhitvāj jñānaliṅgair ivāśritam
english: Even when rightly taught, it is but dimly perceived, as if through swarming bees; the mind bent on action, through want of true insight, seems to take refuge in the mere tokens of knowledge.

sanskrit: idaṃ kāryam idaṃ neti na mokṣeṣūpadiśyate paśyataḥ śṛṇvato buddhir ātmano yeṣu jāyate
english: 'This is to be done, this is not'—such is not taught in the paths of liberation; rather, it lies in those things wherein, as one sees and hears, the understanding of the Self is born.

sanskrit: yāvanta iha śakyeraṃs tāvato 'ṃśān prakalpayet vyaktān avyaktarūpāṃś ca śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: As many portions as can here be conceived, so many let one frame—manifest and unmanifest in form, by hundreds and by thousands.
